title: Boss: onboard a team, rotate nothing
summary: A per-team config built with count: add a team without rotating anyone's database password, give gold teams 24x7 paging with a filtered for_each, and add the guard rails a reviewer would ask for.

steps.title: TEAM-41
body: *"Payments is joining the platform. They need their database password and env file like every other team, and gold
teams get 24x7 paging. Last time someone added a team, two other teams' passwords rotated in the middle of the day."*
`~/infra/teams` is applied. Three steps; each check runs Terraform and compares passwords against what they were.

steps.title: Add payments, rotate nothing
prompt: Do `~/infra/teams/TICKET.txt`: add `payments` (gold, `payments-lead@example.com`), keeping the list sorted.
First see what happens if you just insert it into the list: `terraform plan` (do not apply that!). Then change the
design so each team is keyed by its name, migrate the existing instances without touching them, add payments, and
apply. Only payments' password and env file may be created.

checks.name: no existing password changed
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/teams && for t in checkout search web; do test "$(sed -n 's/^DB_PASSWORD=//p' out/$t/db.env)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/pw-$t)" || { echo "$t changed"; exit 1; }; done
checks.fail: A team's password rotated. Press Reset scenario: use `for_each` keyed by team name and `moved` blocks.

checks.name: payments has its password and env file
instances are keyed by team name
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/teams && terraform state list | grep -q 'random_password.team_db\["payments"\]' && ! terraform state list | grep -q 'team_db\[[0-9]'
checks.fail: `terraform state list` should show `random_password.team_db["checkout"]` and so on, not numeric indexes.

hints: Inserting payments at position 1 shifts search and web: their passwords would be replaced. Turn `var.teams` into a `map(object({ tier = string, owner = string }))` keyed by name.
`for_each = var.teams` on both resources; `each.key` is the team name; reference the password as `random_password.team_db[each.key].result`.

Six `moved` blocks: `[0]` to `["checkout"]`, `[1]` to `["search"]`, `[2]` to `["web"]`, for `random_password.team_db` and for `local_sensitive_file.team_env`. The plan must then say `2 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`.
solution: type = map(object({ tier = string, owner = string }))
steps.explain: The plan: six *has moved to* notes and `2 to add` (payments' password and file). This is the most common Terraform refactor in real repos, and the most common cause of "why did it rotate?" incidents. Anything with an identity gets `for_each`.

steps.title: Paging for gold teams only
prompt: Gold teams get 24x7 paging. In `~/infra/teams`, add a `local_file` named `pager` that writes `out/<team>/pager.yaml`
for **gold teams only**, with the content `escalation: 24x7` and `owner: <the team's owner>` on two lines. Add an
output `pager_files`: a map from team name to the file's path. Apply.

checks.name: gold teams have a pager file
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/teams && for t in checkout payments web; do diff <(printf 'escalation: 24x7\nowner: %s-lead@example.com\n' $t) out/$t/pager.yaml || exit 1; done
checks.fail: `out/<team>/pager.yaml` for checkout, payments and web should hold `escalation: 24x7` and `owner: <owner>`.

checks.name: silver teams do not
checks.fail: `search` is silver: it should have no pager file.

checks.name: pager_files output
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/teams && terraform output -json pager_files | jq -r 'keys | join(",")'
checks.fail: `terraform output -json pager_files` should be a map whose keys are the gold teams.

hints: Filter the map in `for_each`: `{ for name, t in var.teams : name => t if t.tier == "gold" }`.
The output: `{ for name, f in local_file.pager : name => f.filename }`. A resource with `for_each` is itself a map of instances.
solution: for_each = { for name, t in var.teams : name => t if t.tier == "gold" }
value = { for name, f in local_file.pager : name => f.filename }
steps.explain: A filtered `for_each` is how optional per-item resources are written. When search becomes gold, changing one word adds exactly one file. `local_file.pager` used as a value is a map of the instances, which makes the output a one-line `for`.

steps.title: The reviewer's guard rails
prompt: The reviewer asks for two guard rails before this merges:
1. `var.teams`: every `tier` must be `gold` or `silver`, and every `owner` an e-mail address. A typo like
`tier = "glod"` must fail the plan, not silently skip paging.
2. The teams' database passwords must never be destroyed by a plan: refuse it in the code.
Apply what needs applying and leave a clean plan.

checks.name: a typo in tier is refused
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/teams && ! terraform plan -input=false -no-color -var 'teams={checkout={tier="glod",owner="checkout-lead@example.com"}}' > /tmp/o 2>&1 && grep -q 'Invalid value for variable' /tmp/o
checks.fail: A plan with `tier = "glod"` should fail with *Invalid value for variable*.

checks.name: a bad owner is refused
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/teams && ! terraform plan -input=false -no-color -var 'teams={checkout={tier="gold",owner="the checkout lead"}}' > /tmp/o 2>&1 && grep -q 'Invalid value for variable' /tmp/o
checks.fail: A plan with `owner = "the checkout lead"` should fail validation.

checks.name: passwords cannot be destroyed
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/teams && ! terraform plan -destroy -input=false -no-color > /tmp/o 2>&1 && grep -q 'Instance cannot be destroyed' /tmp/o && grep -q 'random_password.team_db' /tmp/o
checks.fail: `terraform plan -destroy` should fail with *Instance cannot be destroyed* for the passwords.

checks.name: still clean
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/teams && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -input=false -no-color >/dev/null && for t in checkout search web payments; do test "$(sed -n 's/^DB_PASSWORD=//p' out/$t/db.env)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/pw-$t)" || exit 1; done
checks.fail: `terraform plan` should show no changes and every password must be unchanged.

hints: Two `validation` blocks on `var.teams`, each with `alltrue([for name, t in var.teams : ...])`.
`lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` in `random_password.team_db`. Run `terraform plan -destroy` to see it refuse.
solution: sed -i '/^  special  = false$/a\  lifecycle {\n    prevent_destroy = true\n  }' main.tf
steps.explain: Validation and lifecycle rules are part of the configuration, not of the state, so nothing needed applying: the plan was clean all along. The reviewer's question behind both: *what is the worst a one-character typo can do here?* Now the answer is: fail a plan.
